sections.content: Before European arrival, America contained very different geographical regions, and formal connectors like a lo *largo* de and *como* *consecuencia* de are useful for describing how geography shaped where people settled.

items.spanish: La cordillera, que atraviesa gran parte del continente, separaba regiones con climas muy distintos.
items.english: The mountain range, which crosses much of the continent, separated regions with very different climates.

items.spanish: A lo largo de la costa las comunidades pescaban, mientras que en el altiplano cultivaban otros productos.
items.english: Along the coast communities fished, while on the high plateau they grew other crops.

items.spanish: Como consecuencia de la diversidad geográfica, cada territorio desarrolló recursos propios.
items.english: As a consequence of the geographic diversity, each territory developed its own resources.

sections.content: A lo *largo* de and *como* *consecuencia* de are formal connectors typical of historical writing — they don't appear much in everyday conversation.
